proof.text: Write the positive coefficient exponent as m+1. The finite-Tor input has intrinsically constructible cohomology and finite homology support. Bound that support above and below, and apply finiteRing_constructibleDerived_origin to obtain a bounded constructible etale representative and its comparison isomorphism. Its lower cohomology bound makes it a DerivedCategory.Plus object. Package the original input, this antecedent, and the actual comparison as a CompactOrigin; the exact comparison functor is definitionally the published origin functor.

The canonical constant-ring pullback compositor supplies the auxiliary coefficient equality for r.hom followed by d.g. Apply finite_ring_refinement_coordinates_canonical to the retained origin, the given open coefficient equality, and this auxiliary equality. Keep its isomorphism and open-unit normalization equation; discard the additional proper-image coordinate equation. The retained origin has underlying object literally the original K, so these are the required endpoints and normalization.

proof_origin.place: First two paragraphs: the canonical proper/open comparison on retained bounded-below etale origins; finite constructible origin is Stacks Tag 09AL.

theorem exists_normalized_refinement_iso_finite
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{max u v}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{max u v}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    {c d : Compactification f} (r : c.Refinement d)
    (E : FieldStage.{max u v} l) (n : ℕ+)
    (hi : ((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l).pull (c.i ≫ r.hom) =
      proEtaleRingCompositeCoefficients c.i r.hom
        (((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l).ring d.Z)
        (((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l).ring c.Z)
        (((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l).ring X)
        (((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l).pull r.hom)
        (((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l).pull c.i))
    (K : C.{u, v} l Ω X (.finite E n)) :
    ∃ ε :
        (PurCompactSupport.openExtension
          ((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l) d.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          ((RingStage.inclusion.{u, v} l Ω X (RingStage.finite E n)).obj K) ≅
        (PurCompactSupport.push ((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l) r.hom).obj
          ((PurCompactSupport.openExtension
            ((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l) c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj
            ((RingStage.inclusion.{u, v} l Ω X (RingStage.finite E n)).obj K)),
      (PurCompactSupport.openDerivedAdjunction
        ((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l) d.i).homEquiv _ _ ε.hom ≫
          PurCompactSupport.refinementRestriction ((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l) r hi
            ((RingStage.inclusion.{u, v} l Ω X (RingStage.finite E n)).obj K) =
        (PurCompactSupport.openDerivedAdjunction
          ((RingStage.finite E n).coefficients l) c.i).unit.app
          ((RingStage.inclusion.{u, v} l Ω X (RingStage.finite E n)).obj K)

title: The finite coefficient normalized refinement comparison exists
statement: For a finite RingStage.finite E n under the ring-stage hypotheses, every finite-Tor input admits the normalized open/proper refinement isomorphism with the displayed transpose equation.
